subject: Cooking
title: Decaf: How They Remove the Buzz
description: Learn Decaf: How They Remove the Buzz in one minute.

hook.text: Decaf coffee still contains caffeine — about 3% remains. And the story of how caffeine gets removed is surprisingly chemical.

buildup.text: Ludwig Roselius invented decaf in 1903 after believing caffeine killed his father.

discovery.text: Modern methods use supercritical CO2 or the Swiss Water Process — chemical-free soaking that selectively removes caffeine.

twist.text: The removed caffeine isn't wasted — it's sold to soft drink and pharmaceutical companies for energy drinks and pills.

climax.text: Scientists have now discovered naturally caffeine-free coffee species in Africa — no decaffeination process needed.

punchline.text: We spent a century removing caffeine. Nature already made coffee without it.

quiz.question: What happens to the caffeine removed during decaffeination?
options: It's sold to soft drink and pharmaceutical companies
It's put back into regular coffee

details.summary: Decaffeination removes 97 percent of caffeine from green coffee beans using one of three methods: chemical solvents like methylene chloride, supercritical CO2 extraction, or the Swiss Water Process that uses only water and osmosis.
details.whyItMatters: Decaf drinkers deserve to know how their coffee is processed. The method significantly affects flavor quality, and the Swiss Water Process or CO2 methods preserve more complexity than solvent methods.
takeaways: Decaf retains about 3 percent of original caffeine content
Swiss Water Process uses no chemicals — only water and osmosis
CO2 extraction preserves the most flavor but is the most expensive

faq.question: Is decaf coffee completely caffeine-free?
faq.answer: No. Regulations require at least 97 percent caffeine removal. A typical decaf cup contains 2 to 15 mg of caffeine compared to 95 to 200 mg in regular coffee. Sensitive individuals may still notice the small remaining amount, especially with multiple cups.

faq.question: Which decaffeination method produces the best-tasting coffee?
faq.answer: Supercritical CO2 extraction is considered best for preserving flavor because it selectively targets caffeine while leaving other compounds intact. Swiss Water Process is close behind and appeals to those wanting chemical-free processing.
